collectibleSets.completionMessage: You found every shell on the harbor beach. What a collection!
Your Firepeak journal page is full of discoveries!
All four elemental crystals are yours!
You found every ember shard on Firepeak!
You found all seven pieces of the Christmas Star!
Ten sparkling snowflakes! Here is a snowflake scarf.
You found every candy cane in the forest!
All three golden bells are jingling together!

items.description: A little shell that curls around and around like a slide.
Pale and round, like a tiny moon washed up on the sand.
Tip it toward the sun and it shows every color at once.
Hold it to your ear and it hums the sound of the sea.
A wide straw hat for shell hunters. Earned by finding every shell.
Pip gave you this for fixing the Moonlight Bridge.
Your own drawings of how bees waggle to share directions.
A feather pen from Keeper Quill, for the tale you helped tell.
A warm, shimmering scale Ember gave you as a thank you.
Pip taught you this knot the day you became friends.
A key carved out of a piece of driftwood, worn smooth by the sea.
A little jar of soft green moss that never stops glowing.
Clear as water, and it catches every light in the room.
An old storybook from the reading nook. The last page is still empty.
items.displayName: The Book with a Blank Page

The bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano, where gas and lava come out.
Melted rock that comes out of the ground. Under the ground it is called magma.
Cracks in the ground that let out steam, heated by magma deep below.
When hot, mineral-rich rock cools slowly, tiny pieces line up and grow into crystals.
A piece of the legendary Heart Crystal. Real crystals form in rock; this one also glows with island magic.
A green crystal from Emberwood Forest. It glows softly with island magic.

Magma is hot melted rock underground. When it comes out of a volcano, it is called lava.
Basalt, pumice and obsidian are igneous rocks. They form when lava cools.
A volcano grows when lava and ash from eruptions pile up in layers and harden.
Some islands, like Hawaii, grew as eruptions built up layers of rock until the volcano rose above the sea.

Water can be ice, liquid water, or a gas called water vapour.
Real stars are huge balls of hot gas, very far away. Our Sun is a star, and the Christmas Star is island magic.

You carry the book with the blank page down the stair with you.
